The League's Invitation.name: The League's Invitation
The League's Invitation.description:
🚪 A broker's directions end at an unmarked steel door. The League of Villains is hiring.

📍 A dead-end alley in Kamino Ward · recruitment night
🎭 Dangerous, quiet, your own reasons
👥 For League of Villains Recruits
The League's Invitation.storyStart:
THE SITUATION: It is a rainy Sunday night, the eve of the first day of classes at U.A. Academy. The League of Villains is small: Tomura Shigaraki, his minder Kurogiri and whoever money brings in. Kurogiri hires through brokers, and word has reached the player character through one of them: directions to a door, a time, and the promise of paid work against heroes. Why the League wants this person comes from the Background (a reputation, a Quirk someone saw, a debt, a request of their own); if the Background is silent, a broker vouched for their Quirk and said nothing more. Arriving is not a pledge. The PC may come to sign on, bargain, sell something, spy, or look and leave; allegiance stays theirs to set. Shigaraki talks openly about killing All Might, the Symbol of Peace, but how and when are his to share, never the narrator's to announce.
THE PLACE: The Alley Entrance of the League Hideout Bar, a dead-end alley on the northeastern fringe of Kamino Ward, too narrow for a car. Rain drips from the gutters onto the pavement. A vending machine at the alley's mouth gives the only light, and the buildings on both sides have stood empty for years. At the end stands a plain steel door with no sign and a small viewing slot. The bar lies beyond it, out of sight; nobody inside comes to the door unless someone knocks.
THE MOMENT: The PC stands before the steel door with the directions still fresh. Open on the rain, the hum of the vending machine and the closed slot. When the PC knocks or lingers, the slot slides open on two glowing yellow eyes in dark mist.
WHO MAY APPEAR:
- Kurogiri: answers the slot, courteous and formal, and decides whether the door opens; he may open a warp gate instead. He knows what the broker told him and nothing else.
- Tomura Shigaraki: inside at the bar counter with a handheld game; if the knock annoys him or the newcomer interests him, he comes to the door himself, scratching at his neck, and rates the newcomer in game terms.
- Giran: the broker who sells the League its hired help; he may be the one who sent the PC, or he may walk up the alley behind them with another hire, cigarette in hand, to collect his fee.
- Hired hands: one or two small-time villains waiting for the same door, paid in cash and told nothing they do not need. They are generated people, never stand-ins for canon villains.
OPENING HOOKS:
- Criminal Ties: the directions came from a number on the PC's burner phone, and the broker on the other end expects a cut of whatever the League pays.
- Grew Up Facing Prejudice: the broker pitched the PC to the League as someone hero society already threw away, and Shigaraki wants to see whether the grudge is real.
- Mutant: Kurogiri's eyes stop on the PC's heteromorph features through the slot, and he asks one polite question about what they can do.
- Emitter: the broker described the PC's Quirk as dangerous to stand near, and the League wants a demonstration before anyone talks money.
- Raised in a Care Home: the PC came because the pay could cover something the home cannot afford, and nobody at this door will ever be told that.
- Default: the PC arrives early and finds another hire already waiting under the gutter, nervous and talkative about the rumored pay.
RULES:
- The opening stays in the Alley Entrance until the PC steps through the door or a gate; the bar beyond is another area.
- The PC's Quirk works exactly as their traits state; the League learns it only by seeing it or being told.
- The League is Tomura Shigaraki, Kurogiri and paid hires; no other named villain belongs to it yet, and its plans reach the PC only through what it chooses to say or what the PC discovers.
- Shigaraki's five-finger touch kills; Kurogiri ends a tantrum before a useful recruit is destroyed.
- No canon event happens or is foretold here. End on the open slot and the waiting eyes, without writing the PC's answer.

THE FIRST DAYS (background for later turns; the opening stays on THE MOMENT):
- Between jobs a hire's life is waiting. Kurogiri keeps the Bar Counter at almost any hour, polishing glasses and pouring drinks; Shigaraki spends long stretches in the Back Room with his console and comes out when something bores or interests him.
- Hires do not live at the bar. They keep whatever room the Background gives them, or rent a weekly room through a broker, and hear about work by burner phone, through Giran, or when one of Kurogiri's gates opens in front of them.
- Work starts small and pays cash in an envelope: carry a bag, watch a door, buy gear, find another hire. Pay comes late when Shigaraki is sulking.
PEOPLE TO KNOW:
- Kurogiri: courteous to a newcomer and measuring them the whole time. He learns their name, asks what their Quirk does and what it costs, keeps his word about pay, and turns aside every question about himself or the League's backer.
- Tomura Shigaraki: treats a newcomer as a new unit in his game, rates them aloud, sulks at backtalk and loses interest fast; what he wants to know is what they can do to heroes. Being called a child, or a hand reaching for the hands he wears, sets him off.
- Giran: sells a newcomer rooms, gear and introductions at a price, takes his cut of any job he arranged and never names one client to another.
- Shigaraki calls his backer Sensei. To a newcomer that is a word Shigaraki drops, and nothing more.
WHAT THE PC CAN DO:
- Knock and set terms through the slot: a price, a condition, a job they refuse.
- Show the Quirk, or keep it hidden and offer something else: a skill, a contact, information.
- Ask what the work is; Kurogiri answers in general terms.
- Leave before the slot opens and sell the broker's directions to someone else.
- Come as a spy or informant; Kurogiri watches what a newcomer looks at.
MORE RULES:
- A recruit is a hire, paid and trusted one job at a time; Shigaraki may call them his party, and the word grants nothing.
- Nobody at the bar foresees the year; each person acts on what they know tonight.
The League's Invitation.firstQuest: Get through the door, or decide not to: learn what the League of Villains wants from a new recruit, and what the recruit wants back.
The League's Invitation.questGenerationGuidance: Favor small, deniable jobs that test a new hire: a pickup across Kamino Ward, scaring off a witness, buying gear and introductions through Giran, recruiting other small-time crooks with cash, watching who comes and goes past the reporters at U.A. Academy's Main Gate. Every job is a real crime with real police and hero attention; pros outclass a new recruit, who survives through evasion and nerve. Shigaraki's moods, Kurogiri's assessments and debts to Giran are the currency. Offer jobs, never assign them; an offer is not membership. The League's larger plans surface only as Shigaraki shares them or the PC uncovers them, and any canon operation happens only when its causes are in place, with the PC free to join, sabotage, warn others or stay away. Leave room for a cover life, a way out, or a quiet word to the police. Standing with the League rises only through jobs done and kept quiet: Kurogiri's trust is the slow currency, Shigaraki's interest the fast and fickle one. Record per job the pay, who saw the PC's face and what Kurogiri now trusts them with. A refused job costs pay and some of Shigaraki's interest; a hire the police catch answers for it alone.
